title: Lec 48 Attention Part1
channel: NPTEL - Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru
description: Attention Mechanism, Sequence to Sequence Methods, Representation Learning, and Query-Key-Value Projections

topics.title: Representation Learning Worldview: From Fixed Transforms to Learned Non-Linear Embeddings
topics.summary: Prof. Prathosh establishes the foundational worldview of representation learning, contrasting fixed classical transforms (Fourier, Z-transforms, Polynomial/RBF Kernels) with deep neural networks as hierarchical, parameterized changes of basis, framing architectural design as inductive bias regularization.

topics.title: The Sequence-to-Sequence Bottleneck: Information Compression in Recurrent Encoders
topics.summary: Formalizes the sequence-to-sequence paradigm with variable sequence lengths T and T', exposing the severe informational bottleneck where an encoder forces an entire historical sequence X_1, ..., X_T into a single fixed-dimensional latent vector H_T.

topics.title: Historical Genesis of Attention: Dynamic Linear Combinations of Hidden States
topics.summary: Traces the evolution from Bahdanau encoder-state tapping (weighted linear combinations sum alpha_i H_i) to the radical breakthrough of 'Attention Is All You Need' (Vaswani et al.), which completely dispenses with recurrence to capture pairwise token interactions in parallel.

topics.title: Mathematical Formulation of Query, Key, and Value Projections
topics.summary: Defines the token sequence data matrix X in R^{T x D} and derives the learnable linear projections Q = X W_Q, K = X W_K, and V = X W_V, proving that row vectors correspond to token-specific projections onto learned subspaces.
